name: quickjs
description: Evaluate JavaScript code and return its completion value (the value of the last expression or statement). Has a scalar form (returns the value converted to VARCHAR; each row runs in a fresh JavaScript context) and a table form (the code must evaluate to an array and each element becomes a row of the JSON column `result`). In the table form extra arguments are available as `arg0`, `arg1`, … and `parsed_arg0` (arg0 parsed as JSON when it is a JSON string, otherwise arg0 itself); the code may contain several statements. A returned Promise is awaited. Execution is bounded by `quickjs_memory_limit`, `quickjs_timeout_ms` and `max_execution_time`, and can be cancelled.

examples.description: Several statements; the last expression is the result
Native list argument and a multi-statement script (DuckDB 2.0 build)
examples.code: SELECT * FROM quickjs('const out = []; for (const x of arg0) out.push({x, square: x * x}); out', [1, 2, 3]);

name: quickjs_eval
description: Call a JavaScript function with the given arguments and return its result as JSON. The first argument is a JS function expression; the remaining arguments are passed positionally as native JavaScript values: integers and DECIMAL as numbers (BIGINT/HUGEINT beyond 2^53 as BigInt), VARCHAR as strings, BOOLEAN as booleans, DATE and TIMESTAMP types as Date, BLOB as Uint8Array, LIST/ARRAY as arrays, STRUCT/MAP as objects, NULL as null; other types arrive as their string form. The result is serialized with JSON.stringify (BigInt as a JSON number); `undefined` returns SQL NULL. Async functions are awaited. The function is compiled once per thread and reused while the script text stays the same.

examples.description: Lists and structs arrive as arrays and objects (DuckDB 2.0 build)
examples.code: SELECT quickjs_eval('(tags, user) => tags.map(t => user.name + ":" + t)', ['a', 'b'], {'name': 'duck'});

examples.description: Dates arrive as JavaScript Date objects (DuckDB 2.0 build)
Custom JSON munging — better than chaining json_extract_*
examples.code: SELECT quickjs_eval('(payload) => { const d = JSON.parse(payload); return { user: d.user, os: d.meta.os }; }', payload) AS extracted FROM events;
SELECT quickjs_eval('(x) => x > 0 ? x : undefined', -1) IS NULL;
